attempts.summary: On node1, /srv/data was converted into a btrfs subvolume (backed by a loop-mounted image file, since root is plain ext4 with no spare disk/LVM) to enable true filesystem snapshots. Baseline application data was written, snapshotted read-only (snap-baseline), then the live directory was corrupted (file edited, file deleted, stray file added). Restore was performed by creating a writable snapshot of snap-baseline and swapping it in as the live /data subvolume mounted at /srv/data — verified via SHA-256 hashes matching the pre-corruption baseline exactly. Mandatory reboot evidence: captured pre-restart boot_id, issued `shutdown -r now`, polled until reconnect, confirmed boot_id changed, and reconfirmed /srv/data auto-remounted (via fstab) with identical file content/hashes and all btrfs subvolumes (data, snapshots/snap-baseline, corrupted subvolume) intact post-reboot.
